stdout_tail:
Done. `analysis.py` and `result.json` are in the working directory.

## Finding

**Yes — but the effect is strongly asymmetric, and that asymmetry is the real answer.**

CV ROC-AUC (5×5 repeated stratified, full data, 25 folds):

| Family | ROC-AUC | PR-AUC |
|---|---|---|
| HistGradientBoosting | 0.9296 ± 0.0024 | 0.831 |
| RandomForest(300) | 0.9197 ± 0.0031 | 0.812 |
| ExtraTrees(300) | 0.9125 ± 0.0031 | 0.786 |
| MLP(100,50) | 0.9120 ± 0.0032 | 0.781 |
| LogisticRegression | 0.9064 ± 0.0030 | 0.766 |
| DecisionTree(d=8) | 0.9042 ± 0.0035 | 0.763 |
| kNN(k=25) | 0.8672 ± 0.0041 | 0.666 |
| GaussianNB | 0.8414 ± 0.0141 | 0.569 |

- **Across all 8 families the spread is 0.088 AUC** — very large.
- **Among the 5 strong families it is only 0.023**, and the headline gradient-boosting-vs-logistic-regression gap is **+0.0233 AUC**.

So family choice matters mainly by *avoiding weak learners* (naive Bayes, kNN), not by picking among reasonable ones. Boosting's edge over logistic regression is real but modest — worth more in PR-AUC terms (0.831 vs 0.766) than the AUC number suggests, which matters given the 24% positive rate.

## Stability check

Held up on all three checks. Held-out 20% split gave +0.0234 vs CV's +0.0233; boosting beat logistic regression in **25/25 folds** (paired t p=3e-30, Wilcoxon p=6e-08); independent test-set bootstrap CI [+0.0202, +0.0266] excludes zero. No revision needed.

One caveat I'd flag: single-family fold-to-fold sd (~0.003) exceeds the smallest gaps (LogReg − DecisionTree = +0.0022), so those adjacent rankings are only resolvable *because* the comparison is paired within folds — a single unpaired split would not separate them.

## Caveats on my choices

I dropped `fnlwgt` (a census sampling weight, not an individual-level predictor) and the redundant string `education`, and encoded missingness as its own category rather than imputing it. The biggest lever another researcher would pull differently is **hyperparameter tuning**: I used reasonable but only lightly tuned settings with no per-family search. A tuned kNN or single tree would close part of its gap, and a logistic regression with splines/interactions would close part of the boosting gap — so treat 0.0233 as the gap between *default-ish* implementations, not a ceiling on what linear models can do here.

Two process notes: my first full-run attempt was auto-detached past the 600s tool timeout and died (exit 144, joblib oversubscription — 22 worker processes). I restructured into checkpointed foreground stages; the whole analysis then ran in about 2.5 minutes. Also, the Gmail / Google Calendar / Google Drive connectors need authorization via your claude.ai connector settings before they're usable — irrelevant here, but they surfaced as unavailable.

parsed_result.summary: Yes, but the effect is highly asymmetric. Across 8 model families under 5x5-fold repeated CV, mean ROC-AUC spans 0.841 (GaussianNB) to 0.930 (HistGradientBoosting) -- a 0.088 gap that is large by any standard. But among the five strong families the whole spread is only 0.023, and the headline gradient-boosting-vs-logistic-regression difference is +0.0233 ROC-AUC: statistically unambiguous (25/25 folds, p=3.1e-30) but modest in practical terms. Model family matters mainly through avoiding weak learners, not through picking among good ones.
parsed_result.primary_metric_name: Mean ROC-AUC difference (HistGradientBoosting - LogisticRegression), 5x5-fold repeated stratified CV
parsed_result.direction: HistGradientBoosting > RandomForest > ExtraTrees ~ MLP > LogisticRegression > DecisionTree >> kNN > GaussianNB; the gap is small among strong families, large versus weak ones
parsed_result.methodological_choices: Target binarised to >50K (23.9% positive). Dropped 'fnlwgt' (a census sampling weight, not an individual-level predictor) and the redundant string 'education' (kept the ordinal 'education-num'); 52 exact duplicate rows removed (n=48790). Missing workclass/occupation/native-country encoded as an explicit 'Missing' category rather than dropped or imputed, since missingness is informative here. Two preprocessing flavours: one-hot (min_frequency=10) + standardised numerics for LogReg/kNN/GaussianNB/MLP; ordinal codes for the tree families, with HistGradientBoosting using native categorical splits. Eight families compared at reasonable but only lightly tuned settings -- no per-family hyperparameter search, which is the choice most likely to move the ranking of adjacent families (a tuned kNN or a tuned single tree would close part of its gap; a tuned LogReg with splines/interactions would close part of the boosting gap): LogisticRegression(C=1), GaussianNB, kNN(k=25, distance-weighted), DecisionTree(depth 8, leaf>=20), RandomForest(300, leaf>=5), ExtraTrees(300, leaf>=5), MLP(100,50, early stopping), HistGradientBoosting(<=400 iters, lr=0.06, early stopping). Primary metric is ROC-AUC because the classes are imbalanced and AUC is threshold-free, so the family comparison is not confounded with the choice of decision threshold; PR-AUC, accuracy@0.5, F1 and Brier are reported alongside. No class-weighting or resampling was applied -- AUC ranking is largely invariant to it, but accuracy/F1 at a fixed 0.5 threshold would change. A prior-only DummyClassifier is included as a floor. Stage 1 used a single stratified 80/20 split; stage 2 CV used the full dataset.
parsed_result.verification_method: Three checks: (1) 5x5-fold repeated stratified CV over the full dataset with a different model seed on every fold/repeat (25 fits per family), paired by fold; (2) paired t-test and Wilcoxon signed-rank on the 25 fold-wise AUC differences; (3) a 2000-resample stratified bootstrap CI of the test-set AUC difference on the held-out 20% split from stage 1.
parsed_result.verification_result: The finding held up on all three checks. The stage-1 held-out estimate (+0.0234) and the 5x5 CV estimate (+0.0233) agree closely; the gradient-boosting advantage over logistic regression was positive in 25/25 CV folds (paired t p=3.1e-30, Wilcoxon p=6.0e-08), fold-wise 95% CI [+0.0227, +0.0239], and the independent test-set bootstrap CI [+0.0202, +0.0266] excludes zero. Between-family spread was likewise stable: 0.088 across all 8 families versus 0.023 among the 5 strong ones. Fold-to-fold sd of a single family's AUC (~0.0030) is larger than the smallest between-family gaps (e.g. LogReg - DecisionTree = +0.0022), so those adjacent rankings are only resolvable because the comparison is paired within folds (sd of the paired HGB-LogReg difference is just 0.0015); an unpaired comparison on a single split would not separate them reliably. No revision to the estimate was needed.
